hypothesis.statement: The two remaining mismatched slots have different causes and only one is a declaration question. (a) Block C (switch case 1, src/game/game/combat.c:2927) seats its `f32 d[3]` at ours r1+72..83 where the target seats it at r1+68..79 with the spare 4 bytes ABOVE it at r1+80..83, so the target's case-1 block declares one more 4-byte object BEFORE d. Adding `u8 unused3[4];` as that block's first declaration is the obvious form and was PROBED THIS RUN and REGRESSED HARD (real 771 -> 899), so the next lane must NOT simply retry it: the 4 bytes have to arrive without perturbing the block's other allocations, e.g. by widening an existing declared object in that block rather than prepending a new one. (b) Target slot r1+20 carries 2 uses and ours carries none anywhere in r1+8..27; since a declared-but-unused pad cannot manufacture USES, this is not a pad at all but either a genuinely unrecovered 4-byte local in the last block or a compiler spill our build keeps in a register, and it should be attacked as a value question, not a layout one.
